OVERVIEW
Akin Wallet, by John Deniel Santos Dela Peña, is an offline vault for your social accounts, bank cards, and Philippine government IDs. There is no online account, no sign-up, and no server. Everything you save stays on this device.

DATA YOU STORE
Only what you type: account usernames, passwords, and PINs; bank and cardholder names, card numbers, expiry dates, CVVs, and card PINs; and the document details for your National ID, Driver's License, Passport, SSS, PhilHealth, or TIN ID. The app adds nothing of its own.

WHAT IS NEVER COLLECTED
No analytics, no crash reports, no advertising identifiers, no location, and no contacts. The app declares no network permission, so the Android system itself prevents it from sending data anywhere. Nothing you store leaves this device through Akin Wallet.

HOW IT IS PROTECTED
The vault is encrypted at rest with AES-256 (SQLCipher). Its key is a random 256-bit value created on this device - never derived from your PIN - and sealed by the hardware-backed Android keystore; only the sealed copy is kept, and the live key exists in memory only. Your 4-digit PIN is never stored: only a salted, computationally slow hash is kept to verify it. Five wrong entries trigger a 30-second lockout, and the app re-locks every time it restarts. Fingerprint unlock stays off unless you turn it on in Settings, and fingerprint data is handled entirely by Android - the app never sees it.

BACKUPS AND LOSS
The encrypted vault and its key are excluded from Google cloud backup and device-to-device transfer, because a copy restored anywhere else could never be decrypted. Keep any records you cannot afford to lose somewhere safe: uninstalling the app, resetting the device, or wiping the device keystore destroys access permanently, and no one - not even the developer - can recover your items afterward.

YOUR CONTROL
Deleting an item moves it to Trash, where you can restore it or delete it forever; permanent deletion also removes its links to other accounts. Uninstalling the app deletes the vault and everything in it.

LIMITS
Encryption defeats raw file reads, but no software protection is absolute: on a compromised or rooted device, stored data can still be exposed. Keep the device itself locked as well.

It provides no financial, legal, or identity services, keeps nothing outside your device, and sends your data nowhere.

ABOUT
Akin Wallet is your private, offline vault for social accounts, bank cards, and Philippine government IDs. No online account, no sign-up, no server: everything stays encrypted on this device.

WHAT'S INSIDE
Social accounts with usernames, passwords, and PINs across a built-in catalog of 40+ platforms, with related accounts linked together; bank cards shown as masked previews; and six Philippine government IDs - National ID, Driver's License, Passport, SSS, PhilHealth, and TIN - each rendered with its true document face.

FEATURES
Find anything instantly with dashboard search that never indexes passwords or PINs. Deleted items wait in Trash until you restore them or delete them forever. Optional fingerprint unlock keeps daily access fast, and your app PIN can be changed anytime in Settings.

HOW IT PROTECTS YOU
The vault is encrypted with AES-256 and opens only with your 4-digit PIN, which is never stored - only a salted, slow hash is kept to verify it. Five wrong entries trigger a 30-second lockout. The app declares no network permission, so it cannot send your data anywhere, and the vault is excluded from cloud and device-transfer backups.

REQUIREMENTS
Akin Wallet needs Android 7.0 or later. Fingerprint unlock appears only on devices with capable hardware, and only after you enable it in Settings.

BUILT WITH
Akin Wallet is built with proven open components: SQLCipher for vault encryption, AndroidX Biometric for fingerprint unlock, and Material components for the interface.

SECURITY
The vault is encrypted with AES-256 and guarded by your 4-digit PIN. The app collects nothing and sends your data nowhere; see the Privacy Policy in Settings for the full details.

DEVELOPER
Designed and built by John Deniel Santos Dela Peña. Contact: johndenieldelapena97@gmail.com.
